nodeData.note: The law of work in Kenya: who is an employee, minimum terms under the Employment Act (Cap. 226, 2007), fair dismissal, unions and strikes, safety, and the ELRC. Sections and figures checked on Kenya Law 10 Nov 2026. A study aid, not legal advice.

children.note: The rules for work: between one worker and an employer, and between unions and employers as groups.
Labour (employment) law sets the rights and duties of employers and workers: pay, hours, safety, leave, discipline and dismissal.

manas.q: What does labour law cover?

children.note: Individual labour law is about one worker's contract. Collective labour law is about trade unions, bargaining and strikes.
A worker usually has less bargaining power than an employer. The law sets minimum terms that a contract cannot go below.
Employment is a contract, so Year 1 Contract ideas apply. Workplace injuries also link to negligence in Torts.
A casual worker on a Nairobi building site paid daily still has legal protection. Which protection depends on how long and how regularly they work.
The first question in most problems: is this person an employee at all? Only employees get most statutory protection.

children.topic: Contract of service vs for services
children.note: An employee works under a contract of service. An independent contractor (like a fundi hired for one job) works under a contract for services.

manas.q: What is the difference between a contract of service and a contract for services?

children.note: A driver who bought his own lorry, paid its costs and was paid per load was held to be a contractor, not an employee, despite wearing the company's colours.
1) The worker gives personal work and skill for pay; 2) the employer has enough control; 3) the other terms fit an employment contract.

manas.q: What three conditions did Ready Mixed Concrete set for a contract of employment?

children.note: Calling someone a 'contractor' in the paperwork does not settle it. Courts look at the real relationship.
Who controls how and when work is done? Who owns the tools? Who bears the risk of loss? Can the worker send a substitute?
Employees get leave, notice, unfair dismissal protection and work injury cover. Contractors mostly rely on their contract alone.
The Employment Act 2007 sets the minimum terms of every employment in Kenya.
The Act sets a floor (s.26). A clause giving a worker less than the Act provides does not remove the statutory right; a more generous CBA, contract or court award wins.

manas.q: Can an employer and worker agree to terms below the Employment Act's minimum?

children.note: A job meant to last three months or more must be in writing (s.9). The written terms (names, job, start date, hours, pay, place of work) must be given within two months of starting (s.10).

manas.q: When must a Kenyan employment contract be in writing?

children.note: A casual worker who works continuously for the equivalent of a month, or on work that cannot be finished within three months, is treated as monthly paid, with the 28-day notice rule (s.37).

manas.q: When does a casual worker become a monthly employee under s.37?

children.note: Wages are paid in Kenyan currency: cash, bank account, cheque or to a person the worker authorises in writing, on a working day (s.17). Unlawful deductions are not allowed; minimum wages come from wage orders.

After every twelve months of service, at least 21 working days' leave with full pay (s.28(1)(a)). If the job ends after two or more months, leave accrues at 1.75 days per completed month. The employer may split it with the worker's consent.

manas.q: How much paid annual leave must a Kenyan employee get after 12 months' service?

children.note: Three months' maternity leave on full pay, with the right to return to the same or a comparable job (s.29(1)-(2)); the worker gives at least seven days' written notice (s.29(4)-(5)). Two weeks' paternity leave on full pay (s.29(8)). Pre-adoptive leave: one month (s.29A).

manas.q: How long are maternity and paternity leave under the Employment Act?

children.note: After two months' service: seven days' sick leave on full pay, then seven days on half pay, in each twelve months, with a medical certificate (s.30). At least one rest day in every seven (s.27).

manas.q: How much paid sick leave does the Employment Act give?

children.note: No direct or indirect discrimination or harassment on race, colour, sex, language, religion, opinion, nationality, ethnic or social origin, disability, pregnancy, marital status or HIV status (s.5(3)); equal pay for work of equal value (s.5(5)). Affirmative action and inherent job requirements are allowed (s.5(4)).

manas.q: Name five prohibited grounds of discrimination in s.5 of the Employment Act.

children.note: How a job can lawfully end, and what makes a dismissal unfair. This is the most examined area.

Daily paid: ends at the close of any day. Paid at intervals under a month: notice equal to that period. Monthly or longer: 28 days' written notice (s.35(1)). The contract may set a longer notice. Either side may pay in lieu of notice (s.36).

manas.q: What is the minimum notice for a monthly paid employee in Kenya?

children.note: A termination is unfair if the employer cannot prove a valid reason, that it was a fair reason (conduct, capacity, compatibility or operational requirements) AND that a fair procedure was followed (s.45(2)). The court also asks whether the employer acted with justice and equity (s.45(4)-(5)).

manas.q: What two things must an employer show for a termination to be fair?

children.note: Before dismissal for misconduct, poor performance or incapacity the employer must explain the reason in a language the worker understands, with a fellow employee or union representative present, and must hear and consider the worker's answer (s.41).

manas.q: What does s.41 require before a dismissal for misconduct?

children.note: In any claim about a termination the employer must prove the reason; if it cannot, the termination is deemed unfair (s.43(1)). The reason is what the employer genuinely believed at the time (s.43(2)).

manas.q: Who bears the burden of proving the reason for termination?

children.note: Dismissal without notice is allowed only where the worker has fundamentally breached the contract (s.44(3)). The Act lists examples of gross misconduct: absence without leave, being drunk at work, wilful neglect, abusive language, failing to obey lawful orders, arrest for a cognisable offence, dishonesty (s.44(4)). A hearing is still required (s.41(2)).

manas.q: Give three examples of gross misconduct listed in s.44(4).

children.note: The worker resigns because the employer committed a serious breach of the contract. Western Excavating v Sharp: use the contract test, not just 'unreasonable'.

manas.q: What is constructive dismissal?

children.note: Redundancy is lawful only if s.40 is met: a month's written notice to the union and labour officer (or the worker personally and the labour officer); fair selection with regard to seniority, skill, ability and reliability; leave paid out; one month's notice or pay; severance.

manas.q: What must an employer do in a redundancy?

children.note: Severance of at least fifteen days' pay for each completed year of service (s.40(1)(g)). A CBA may give more: in the Kenya Airways case the agreed rate was 20 days a year.

Where a dismissal is unfair the court may award notice pay, wages for days worked, compensation of up to twelve months' gross pay (s.49(1)), or order reinstatement or re-engagement (s.49(3)). Reinstatement is rare: s.49(4)(d) keeps the common-law rule against forcing a contract of service.

manas.q: What is the maximum compensation for unfair termination under s.49?

children.note: At the end of employment, the worker is entitled to a certificate of service showing the period worked.

A probationary contract may last up to six months, extendable once by up to six months with the worker's agreement (s.42(2)). Either side may end it on seven days' notice or pay (s.42(4)); the s.41 hearing does not apply (s.42(1)). Checked on Kenya Law 10 Nov 2026; check the current Act.

manas.q: How long may probation last under the Employment Act?

children.topic: Thirteen months to claim unfair termination
children.note: Only a worker continuously employed for at least thirteen months before the termination may complain of unfair termination under s.45 (s.45(3)). Shorter service still allows claims for notice pay and wrongful dismissal. Checked on Kenya Law 10 Nov 2026; check the current Act.

manas.q: How long must a worker have served to claim unfair termination under s.45?

children.note: Pregnancy, taking leave, union membership or activity, refusing to join a union, race, tribe, sex, religion, political opinion, nationality, social origin, disability, HIV status, or filing a complaint against the employer (s.46).

manas.q: Name four reasons s.46 says can never justify dismissal.

children.note: A dismissed worker may complain to a labour officer within three months of the dismissal (s.47(1)); the officer hears both sides and recommends a settlement under s.49. Court claims have their own limitation period: check the ELRC Act and the current rules.
Collective labour law, mainly under the Labour Relations Act.
Workers may form and join trade unions; employers may form employers' organisations. No one can be victimised for union membership.
Covers registration of unions and employers' organisations, recognition, collective agreements, and disputes and strikes.
An employer must recognise a union that represents a simple majority of the unionisable employees for bargaining.
A written deal on pay and terms negotiated between a union and employer. Once registered it binds both sides.

manas.q: What is a collective bargaining agreement?

children.note: A trade dispute is first reported for conciliation. Only if that fails can parties strike, lock out or go to court.
A strike is protected only if the proper steps and notice are followed. Workers in essential services face extra limits.
Health workers' strikes in Kenya show the tension between the right to strike and patients' right to care. Courts often order talks to resume.
Keeping workers safe, and compensating them when they are hurt.
Requires employers to provide a safe workplace, safe machinery, training and protective gear, and allows workplace inspections.
Workers must take care for their own safety and others', and use the protective equipment provided.
Gives compensation to employees injured or made ill by their work, without needing to prove the employer was negligent.

manas.q: What is the main idea of the Work Injury Benefits Act?

children.note: An injury must be reported to the employer and the Director of Occupational Safety and Health Services, who assesses compensation.

children.topic: Link to the law of torts
children.note: A worker may also have a claim in negligence. Exam answers should mention both routes and how they differ.
Labour rights are constitutional rights in Kenya, with their own specialised court.
Every person has the right to fair labour practices.

manas.q: What right does Article 41(1) give every person?

children.note: Workers have rights to fair pay, reasonable working conditions, to form and join a trade union, and to go on strike.

manas.q: List the four workers' rights in Article 41(2).

children.note: Employers may form and join employers' organisations. Unions and employers' bodies run their own affairs, and all may bargain collectively.
The Constitution told Parliament to set up a court with the status of the High Court for employment and labour disputes.

manas.q: Which court hears employment disputes in Kenya, and what is its status?

children.note: Set up by its own Act, it hears all employment and labour relations disputes. Appeals go to the Court of Appeal. Ordinary High Court is not the forum.
Employment Act 2007, Labour Relations Act, Labour Institutions Act, Occupational Safety and Health Act, Work Injury Benefits Act, Employment and Labour Relations Court Act.
Decisions read on kenyalaw.org on 10 Nov 2026. Each note is our own summary; open the link for the judgment.

A manager was let go with one month's pay under a notice clause. The Supreme Court held that however a termination is done, once a court finds it unfair or wrongful, the s.49 remedies apply; the judge's discretion on the amount is guided by s.49(4). The 12 months' award stood.

manas.q: Kenfreight v Nguti: can a termination by notice still attract s.49 compensation?

children.note: A payment made under an established company practice was held to be an entitlement, not a gift, and was separate from the s.49 award.

In CMC Aviation (CA 2015) only one month's pay was awarded for an unfair termination. The Supreme Court said the two outcomes were not inconsistent: the amount is a matter of judicial discretion within s.49.

A teacher was summarily dismissed over an impostor who sat an exam in his name. The court found a genuine reason but an incomplete investigation: fairness needs both substantive justification and procedural fairness. Dismissal unfair; eight months' pay plus a month's notice pay.

manas.q: Walter Anuro v TSC: what two things must a fair termination show?

children.note: Reinstatement is a special remedy of the labour court, but s.49(4)(d) keeps the common-law rule against specific performance of a contract of service, so it is granted only in exceptional cases.
The claim for severance pay failed: severance under s.40 belongs to redundancy, not to other dismissals.

children.topic: Kenya Airways v Aviation Workers Union (CA 2014)
children.note: KQ declared 447 staff redundant. The Court of Appeal accepted the financial justification but held that s.40(1)(c) was not followed: workers must be assessed on seniority, skill, ability and reliability together, and 'last in first out' alone is not the test. Reinstatement was set aside; six months' pay each instead.

manas.q: Kenya Airways v AAWU: is 'last in first out' the only lawful selection rule in a redundancy?

children.note: The court doubted that Kenyan law makes consultation with the Ministry of Labour mandatory, but notice to the union and labour officer under s.40(1)(a) is required.
Three months' notice pay and 20 days' severance a year came from the CBA clause, showing how a CBA can improve on the Act's 15-day minimum.

A building contractor trespassed on a neighbour's land while working for KPC. The Court of Appeal applied the control, integration, economic-reality and mutuality tests and the s.2 definition of 'employee' and held the contractor was independent, so KPC was not vicariously liable.

manas.q: Kenya Pipeline v Ndegwa: which tests decide employee or independent contractor?

children.topic: Why status matters beyond the ELRC
children.note: The same employee-or-contractor question decides vicarious liability in tort, not only Employment Act rights. See the Torts map.
International labour standards that Kenya takes into account.
A UN agency founded in 1919 and based in Geneva. It sets labour standards through conventions.

manas.q: When was the ILO founded and where is it based?

children.note: Governments, employers and workers all have a voice at the ILO. Kenya's own labour bodies follow the same three-way model.
Freedom of association and collective bargaining; no forced labour; no child labour; no discrimination at work.

manas.q: What four principles does the ILO's 1998 Declaration set out?

children.note: Examples: C87 (freedom of association), C98 (collective bargaining), C29 (forced labour), C138 and C182 (child labour).
Under Article 2(6) of the Constitution, conventions Kenya has ratified form part of Kenyan law, so ILO standards can be argued in court.
IRAC with a Kenyan example, then the mistakes examiners look for.
For example: was Achieng's dismissal from a Kisumu supermarket fair?
Employment Act 2007: valid reason plus fair procedure, with the burden on the employer. Mention Article 41.
She was dismissed by SMS for alleged theft, with no hearing. Even if theft is gross misconduct, the procedure was unfair.
Likely unfair termination. Remedies before the ELRC: compensation (up to 12 months' pay) or reinstatement, plus notice pay.
Always check first whether the person is an employee. Contractors do not get most Employment Act protections.
A good reason does not cure an unfair process. Examine both.
Employment disputes go to the ELRC, not the ordinary High Court.
English cases help on common-law tests, but Kenyan statutes govern. Say plainly where Kenyan law differs.
Short scenarios to answer with IRAC. The answer is the flashcard; the law is in the bubbles above.
Amina, a cashier for three years, gets a WhatsApp message: 'Do not come back, till is short.' No meeting. Fair?

manas.q: Problem 1 answer: Even if the shortage is a valid reason, no s.41 explanation or hearing was given, so the termination is procedurally unfair (s.45(2)(c)); the employer must also prove the reason (s.43). Remedies under s.49: notice pay and up to 12 months' compensation (Walter Anuro).

children.note: Brian has worked ten months when he is terminated without a reason. Can he claim unfair termination?

manas.q: Problem 2 answer: s.45(3) requires thirteen months' continuous service for an unfair-termination complaint. He can still claim notice pay under s.35-36 and wrongful dismissal if the contract was broken; the employer must still prove the reason if challenged (s.43).

children.note: A factory keeps the twenty longest-serving workers and lets the rest go, with 15 days' severance a year. Lawful?

manas.q: Problem 3 answer: s.40(1)(c) requires regard to seniority AND skill, ability and reliability; seniority alone is not a fair selection (Kenya Airways v AAWU). Also check the month's notice to the union/labour officer, leave paid out and notice pay. Severance at 15 days meets the minimum unless a CBA gives more.

children.note: Chege rides a delivery motorbike owned by a company, wears its uniform, works set hours and is paid weekly, but his contract calls him an 'independent partner'. Status?

manas.q: Problem 4 answer: Labels do not decide. Control (hours, uniform, bike), integration into the business, economic reality and mutual obligations (Ready Mixed Concrete; Kenya Pipeline v Ndegwa) point to a contract of service, so the Employment Act minimums and the ELRC apply.
